note: Expected profile detection for tests/fixtures/nc/owner-public: the owner's own programs, published
by him and cleared for public use (plan §9.2, D45). Read by src/lib/core/profiles/detect.test.ts and
src/lib/data/profiles/fanucLathe.test.ts like every other folder's table.
A value is the profile the program has to open with: the profile of the control it was written for,
or, where gEdit has only the turning profile of that control, that profile. The Okuma milling
programs therefore expect okuma-osp, which is what they get; that the turning profile then misreads
them is an outline gap (expected/outline/owner-public/_known-gaps.json), not a detection one.
'knownGaps' lists the programs gEdit detects wrongly today, with the reason. Their entry above is
still the right answer, never what gEdit answers: detect.test.ts runs them as expected failures, so
the day one is fixed its test fails and the entry has to be removed. fanucLathe.test.ts leaves them
out of the margin table, because there the winner is the wrong profile.
'ownerReviewed' stays false until the owner has read these answers (§9.2, owner-public intake step 2).

knownGaps.nc/owner-public/heidenhain-klartext/5X_M: Opens as Fanuc (ISO) mill despite .H and BEGIN PGM: its LN blocks score nothing for Klartext and one point each for the mill's Y rule, so 400 LN lines outvote the extension and the header.
knownGaps.nc/owner-public/sinumerik/2.5D_Milling.m: A Siemens milling program: opens as Fanuc (ISO) mill, because the Sinumerik profile leaves out every line that moves Y (docs/user/dialects.md, Milling on Okuma and Sinumerik).
knownGaps.nc/owner-public/sinumerik/5X_Milling.mpf: A Siemens milling program: opens as Fanuc (ISO) mill, as 2.5D_Milling.mpf.
knownGaps.nc/owner-public/sinumerik/Demo_1.mpf: A Siemens milling program without the %_N_ header: opens as Fanuc (ISO) mill.
